summary: Feed s052_single to SIEM is degraded due to 2.1% packet drops (52 of 2419 TCP packets) exceeding 1% threshold. No duplicates, one-way, VLAN, encryption or tool overload issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Upstream loss before the SIEM - 2.1% of TCP packets show gaps/retransmissions indicating SPAN oversubscription or packet broker buffer overflow. Tool overload check is healthy and port is 1Gbps, so drops occur at the TAP/SPAN or broker aggregation stage, not at the tool itself.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete flows/events; correlation, alerting and forensic timeline have gaps, increasing risk of missed detections even though SIEM does not require full payload or bidirectional traffic.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM needs_full_payload=false, so truncating packets to headers/metadata (e.g., 256 bytes) on the packet broker preserves detection-relevant data while sharply reducing bandwidth and buffer pressure to eliminate the 2.1% drops.
